Western Cape Anti-Gang Unit

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
can the new gang squad make a dent?

Unique Selling Point:
The cape flats is a war zone. Gang-related murders in the Western Cape significantly exceed the trend countrywide, Major-General Norman Sekhukhune, head of police crime research and statistics, announced on Tuesday. The statistics cover the period 1 April, 2017 to 31 March, 2018.
Out of the 973 gang-related crimes committed countrywide, 808 occurred in the Western Cape, with the Eastern Cape markedly lower in second place at 87. They are followed by the Free State with 46 and Gauteng with 14.
In the last two weeks, there have been 18 gang related murders.
Adults and children who live is the Cape Flats are traumatised. One report released a couple of years by the cape Town trauma centre stated that –
Sixty percent of children said they were “jumpy or easily startled”, 55% felt “irritable” and had “fits of anger” and over half said they were not able to concentrate, which “adversely affects school performance”.
The authors note that “traumatised children [are] vulnerable to school failure and drop outs” and those who “drop out of school are at greater risk of gang involvement, criminal activity”, exposure to violence and becoming perpetrators of violence themselves.
We spend an evening with the gang unit and interview Major General Andre Lincoln, who head it up, and our questions will surround: the squads success’s – its challenges, what their goals are, the intelligence work that need to go into operations – what are the solutions besides police activity? Hopefully we will identify a force member who lives on the Cape Flats and who can give his perspective.
We are awaiting confirmation to interview a gangster with a balaclava who can shed light on the rising numbers of gang related deaths.
To help describe the anguish, we speak to acclaimed singer James Bhemgee, who two years ago, survived a gang shooting, and who lost his son and sister recently. James said that gangsters broke into his sister’s home and shot her, and he said that his son was shot en route to a peace meeting.
In response to the violence, a program called Peace Ambassadors was established. It was set up by Professor Brian Williams (UWC) who mediates in war torn countries. He also has a PHD in economics and has a good grasp and gangs and their economies’ (drugs, sex workers etc). The program has been piloted in Cape Town. Teenagers have choices besides being lured into the glamour of gangs. It starts from within - Peace, a state of harmony, is likened to a light that is a gift. This gift must be shared with others for its power to warm the hearts of everyone and to act as a divine compass. The methodologies applied during the peace training demonstrated that it was possible for anyone to become a messenger of peace. Peace has spiritual, philosophical and practical value at personal and collective levels.
we speak to a reformed feared ex gang leader who was 25 years in prison and who now peace ambassador. His name is Magadien Wentzel.

We speak to one 18 year old Riedwaan Samuls who was shot by gangsters while playing soccer. He survived 4 bullets. He is a peace ambassador and instead becoming bitter, he continues to preach peace.

If there is time we speak to the parents of another peace ambassador whose son was killed in cross fire.
As part of a group of peace ambassadors in Hanover Park, Keagan de Silver, 17, was involved in educating his community about the benefits of peace. On Wednesday, the Grade 11 pupil from Mount View High School was shot five times in a spaza shop close to home. His mother, Natasha Williams, said emergency services took their time in taking him to hospital. He took his last breath while she was holding him.

Script:


This is the new police anti-gang unit that was established in the Western Cape to
take down gangsters and smash their underground economy. Heading up the unit is
Major General Andre Lincoln, once President Mandela’s personal body guard. He’s
relishing this new position.
General: I come from the cape flats, I know the suffering and the pain, it really
overjoyed me that I can make a difference.
The general has a daunting task. The Cape Flats have (has) been described as a
war zone as turf battles rage between feuding gangs.
LINK
Around the country we are stunned by the crime statistics. But it come to
gang related crime and murder, nothing comes close to the cape flats.
Of the 973 gang murders committed country wide since April 2017 and March 2018,
808 occurred in the western cape. In the last few months, at leaste 51 people have
been killed. Innocent residents and children are often caught in the cross fire.
Joshua was the apple of his father’s eye.
Johnny:: oh, he was like a peaceful child, running around. he brought so much
light to the family.
Johnny, his wife and family live in this informal settlement in Athlone. On the 4 th of
March around 10 am young GANGSTERS entered the informal settlement.
Community worker Mietah Hofstander spotted them and became suspicious.
Mietha: I went to one of the committee leaders and said that something
community that something was going on here.
Mietah was right – the area was soon rocked by gunfire.
Johnny: I heard three shots
One bullet passed through the front door of Johnny’s home.
Johnny: as I was trying to protect him, to cover the child, so my child was
already hit in the head. So, me and him fall here.
Johnny and Mietha flagged down a motorist who rushed Joshua to hospital… but the
young boy succumbed to his injuries.
Jonny: doctors said that he died, I broke down in tears. My boy
General: you know, one kind of gets used to people being shot, but everytime
a child gets hurt, it drives home an arrow right through your heart.

For decades gangs have terrorised the Cape Flats – but a previous specialised
police gang unit was suddenly shut down in 2012.
De Klerk: no one really knows, at the time it was said that the police was
restructuring at the time, also the gang phoneme, the police felt that they had
arrested the problem.
Eldred de Klerk is a policing analyst and conflict resolution specialist.
De Klerk: what they were doing of course is disrupting gangs and undermining
them, what they were not tackling was the criminal underground.
The Cape Metro’s gang unit has tried to fill the void and Premier Zille demanded
intervention from police minister Bheki Cele.
Sound up: “the minister makes an urgent commitment of additional police to
the western cape”
Zille has also called for the army to be deployed to stem the bloodshed.
But on 20 November last year the new Anti-Gang Unit was announced at a special
ceremony in Hanover Park, a known gang hotspot.
Derek : How does this unit differ to the old gang unit.
General: We don’t associate at all with them, we have visible policing,
detectives and intelligence…our key focus with the anti-gang unit is to deal
with the issue of the criminal underground economy. That is where the power
of the gang is,..not on the street.
Derek: You talk about millions, billions?
General: Billions
Every night either the general or another officer briefs team leaders on the night’s
mission.
Sound up: we going to focus on three areas..Kraaifontien, Kleinvlei and Good
wood.
The whole unit is then addressed before they head out. At present there are around
200 personel in the unit.
Tonight, officers are hoping to arrest a prominent gang leader, a gangster selling
firearms, and drug dealers.
The unit is concentrating on 16 main areas of the Cape Flats and surrounds.

Armed with a search warrant, officers swoop on a house in Goodwood to arrest the
gang leader – but he’s eluded them.
General “ a very well known suspect frequents this house..its his girls friends
mothers house and we know after a shooting he comes here to hide, and he
brings his drugs. He is a real problem”
Two women living at the back of the property are arrested for drug possession.
Later that night drugs are found at another residence, and a gangster is arrested.
Within a month of its inception the new unit arrested 120 suspects for crimes ranging
from murder, attempted murder, procession of stolen property to drug poession or
dealing. 35 of those arrested were gang leaders. And this is just the beginning says
the general,
Derek: what are your challenges General
General. Our challenge is that we are new – and we are in a hurry because of
the deaths we see on the Cape Flats….we want to create an informer network
as fast as possible and second to none. It’s a challenge though
Link: The police can only do so much, and eradicating and diminishing
gangsters on the Cape Flats requires a holistic approach. We are about to
meet the peace ambassadors at a training session. P
One approach that gives an alternative to violence is a program that is being rolled
out in Hanover Park – to date 500 young people have been trained as Peace
Ambassadors .
Prof: Part of my work in Africa and now South Africa is about peace. I believe
that peace can be transformative power.
The programme is the brainchild of Prof Brian Williams who mediates in war torn
counties in Africa. He says that participants, many of whom are traumatized, need to
first find balance first with in themselves
Prof: inner peace is crucial to understanding to get balance and centredness,
so that centredness will help them in dealing with others.
Participants come up with their own definitions of peace and then spread the word in
their communities. But being a peace ambassador does not shield them from
danger. Already one young ambassador was killed in cross fire…but Riedwaan
Samuels was luckier. Last year he was playing soccer on this pitch in Hanover Park
when a gangster appeared from nowhere.
Ridwaan: He shot me four times, first two in the back, then my arm and then
foot.
Riedwaan spend several months recovering in hospital and then returned to the
peace ambassador program even more determined to work for peace

Ridwaan: it educated me to say although this bad thing happened to me, there
are other solutions than violence.
Also in the program are gangsters who are trying to turn their lives around. Clinton
has a long history of violence.
Clinton: I have shot many.
Presenter: how many?
Clinton: I can’t even count…I am not proud

The support he’s received from the programme’s participants has amazed him.
Clinton: its helping me a lot to see that there are still people who care for
people like us…its helping me a lot, as I am thinking more clearer, Lovely that
they accept me, I am thinking clearly now, I have a better vision for me, and I
am getting more power to achieve that.
The Peace Ambassador Program is just one example of how the community is
searching for alternatives to violence. Addressing gangsterism needs everyone’s
input.
De Klerk. It’s not just about crime and criminality and the work of the gang
unit…it needs a multi-disciplinary and agency approach: Civilians, state and
private section.
General: This is not a police problem, it’s everybody’s problem.
Major General Lincoln is determined to be part of the solution.
Derek: Do your men share the same enthusiasm?
General: yes it does, but more than that, we have a togetherness where we are
saying to everybody we are going to change the way we do policing in SA>

But on 20 November last year the new Anti-Gang Unit was announced at a special ceremony in Hanover Park, a known gang hotspot. Derek : How does this unit differ to the old gang unit. General: We don’t associate at all with them, we have visible policing, detectives and intelligence…our key focus with the anti-gang unit is to deal with the issue of the criminal underground economy. That is where the power of the gang is,..not on the street. Derek: You talk about millions, billions? General: Billions Every night either the general or another officer briefs team leaders on the night’s mission. Sound up: we going to focus on three areas..Kraaifontien, Kleinvlei and Good wood. The whole unit is then addressed before they head out. At present there are around 200 personel in the unit. Tonight, officers are hoping to arrest a prominent gang leader, a gangster selling firearms, and drug dealers. The unit is concentrating on 16 main areas of the Cape Flats and surrounds. Armed with a search warrant, officers swoop on a house in Goodwood to arrest the gang leader – but he’s eluded them. General “ a very well known suspect frequents this house..its his girls friends mothers house and we know after a shooting he comes here to hide, and he brings his drugs. He is a real problem” Two women living at the back of the property are arrested for drug possession. Later that night drugs are found at another residence, and a gangster is arrested. Within a month of its inception the new unit arrested 120 suspects for crimes ranging from murder, attempted murder, procession of stolen property to drug poession or dealing. 35 of those arrested were gang leaders. And this is just the beginning says the general, Derek: what are your challenges General General. Our challenge is that we are new – and we are in a hurry because of the deaths we see on the Cape Flats….we want to create an informer network as fast as possible and second to none. It’s a challenge though Link: The police can only do so much, and eradicating and diminishing gangsters on the Cape Flats requires a holistic approach. We are about to meet the peace ambassadors at a training session. P One approach that gives an alternative to violence is a program that is being rolled out in Hanover Park – to date 500 young people have been trained as Peace Ambassadors . Prof: Part of my work in Africa and now South Africa is about peace. I believe that peace can be transformative power. The programme is the brainchild of Prof Brian Williams who mediates in war torn counties in Africa. He says that participants, many of whom are traumatized, need to first find balance first with in themselves Prof: inner peace is crucial to understanding to get balance and centredness, so that centredness will help them in dealing with others. Participants come up with their own definitions of peace and then spread the word in their communities. But being a peace ambassador does not shield them from danger. Already one young ambassador was killed in cross fire…but Riedwaan Samuels was luckier. Last year he was playing soccer on this pitch in Hanover Park when a gangster appeared from nowhere. Ridwaan: He shot me four times, first two in the back, then my arm and then foot. Riedwaan spend several months recovering in hospital and then returned to the peace ambassador program even more determined to work for peace Ridwaan: it educated me to say although this bad thing happened to me, there are other solutions than violence. Also in the program are gangsters who are trying to turn their lives around. Clinton has a long history of violence. Clinton: I have shot many. Presenter: how many? Clinton: I can’t even count…I am not proud The support he’s received from the programme’s participants has amazed him. Clinton: its helping me a lot to see that there are still people who care for people like us…its helping me a lot, as I am thinking more clearer, Lovely that they accept me, I am thinking clearly now, I have a better vision for me, and I am getting more power to achieve that. The Peace Ambassador Program is just one example of how the community is searching for alternatives to violence. Addressing gangsterism needs everyone’s input. De Klerk. It’s not just about crime and criminality and the work of the gang unit…it needs a multi-disciplinary and agency approach: Civilians, state and private section. General: This is not a police problem, it’s everybody’s problem. Major General Lincoln is determined to be part of the solution. Derek: Do your men share the same enthusiasm? General: yes it does, but more than that, we have a togetherness where we are saying to everybody we are going to change the way we do policing in SA>

metadata.Unique Selling Point: The cape flats is a war zone. Gang-related murders in the Western Cape significantly exceed the trend countrywide, Major-General Norman Sekhukhune, head of police crime research and statistics, announced on Tuesday. The statistics cover the period 1 April, 2017 to 31 March, 2018. Out of the 973 gang-related crimes committed countrywide, 808 occurred in the Western Cape, with the Eastern Cape markedly lower in second place at 87. They are followed by the Free State with 46 and Gauteng with 14. In the last two weeks, there have been 18 gang related murders. Adults and children who live is the Cape Flats are traumatised. One report released a couple of years by the cape Town trauma centre stated that – Sixty percent of children said they were “jumpy or easily startled”, 55% felt “irritable” and had “fits of anger” and over half said they were not able to concentrate, which “adversely affects school performance”. The authors note that “traumatised children [are] vulnerable to school failure and drop outs” and those who “drop out of school are at greater risk of gang involvement, criminal activity”, exposure to violence and becoming perpetrators of violence themselves. We spend an evening with the gang unit and interview Major General Andre Lincoln, who head it up, and our questions will surround: the squads success’s – its challenges, what their goals are, the intelligence work that need to go into operations – what are the solutions besides police activity? Hopefully we will identify a force member who lives on the Cape Flats and who can give his perspective. We are awaiting confirmation to interview a gangster with a balaclava who can shed light on the rising numbers of gang related deaths. To help describe the anguish, we speak to acclaimed singer James Bhemgee, who two years ago, survived a gang shooting, and who lost his son and sister recently. James said that gangsters broke into his sister’s home and shot her, and he said that his son was shot en route to a peace meeting. In response to the violence, a program called Peace Ambassadors was established. It was set up by Professor Brian Williams (UWC) who mediates in war torn countries. He also has a PHD in economics and has a good grasp and gangs and their economies’ (drugs, sex workers etc). The program has been piloted in Cape Town. Teenagers have choices besides being lured into the glamour of gangs. It starts from within - Peace, a state of harmony, is likened to a light that is a gift. This gift must be shared with others for its power to warm the hearts of everyone and to act as a divine compass. The methodologies applied during the peace training demonstrated that it was possible for anyone to become a messenger of peace. Peace has spiritual, philosophical and practical value at personal and collective levels. we speak to a reformed feared ex gang leader who was 25 years in prison and who now peace ambassador. His name is Magadien Wentzel. We speak to one 18 year old Riedwaan Samuls who was shot by gangsters while playing soccer. He survived 4 bullets. He is a peace ambassador and instead becoming bitter, he continues to preach peace. If there is time we speak to the parents of another peace ambassador whose son was killed in cross fire. As part of a group of peace ambassadors in Hanover Park, Keagan de Silver, 17, was involved in educating his community about the benefits of peace. On Wednesday, the Grade 11 pupil from Mount View High School was shot five times in a spaza shop close to home. His mother, Natasha Williams, said emergency services took their time in taking him to hospital. He took his last breath while she was holding him. The cape flats is a war zone.
